steps.label: open the Tiles tab
steps.goal: everything in the first half happens there, and the key list changes with the tab. The tab opens on your tiles — the list, not a blank tile; a tile opens when you press Enter on a row
do: press 2
steps.recovery: if a text field has the keyboard the number types into it: press Escape first

steps.label: bring a floor in
steps.goal: a tile with nothing in it has no size and no edges, so the floor comes first
do: walk the list with up and down -- Shift strides five
press Enter on site/floor
steps.checkpoint: the tile has a piece in it
steps.recovery: if the list looks wrong, press F, clear the filter with Backspace, then Enter to hand the keyboard back

steps.label: bring a wall in as well
steps.goal: two pieces is where a tile stops being a mesh with extra steps -- and the arrows will not walk the list while a piece is in hand
do: press Escape to put the floor down
walk to site/wall
press Enter
steps.recovery: if the arrows move the piece instead of the list, Escape did not land -- the panel says which of the two states the tab is in

steps.label: push the wall with EVERY arrow
steps.goal: this is the fix this session is really asking about. All four arrows used to be claimed and only some moved the piece. Press each one several times and watch whether the wall answers every press, in the direction the key names
do: press up, then down, then left, then right -- several of each
watch the wall, not the list
steps.recovery: if an arrow does nothing, say which one and what the tile had in it -- that is the report

steps.label: does the wall reach its own centre
steps.goal: J deepens the step ladder and wraps. A nudge is supposed to land ON a rung, so the tile's centre and its flush edge are both exactly reachable rather than straddled
do: press J to change the step, then walk the wall with the arrows
try to land it dead centre, and then flush against a side
press J again -- three depths, then it wraps
steps.recovery: if centre or flush is unreachable at any depth, that is the report -- say which depth and which target

steps.label: start a new tile and name it
steps.goal: naming became explicit this session: N opens a name PROMPT rather than silently inheriting the kit's name. What you type is what the tile is called
do: press N
type a name
press Enter
steps.recovery: Escape closes the prompt without starting the tile. If the keystrokes went to the map instead of the box, that is the report

steps.label: put a floor and a wall in this one and save it
steps.goal: a saved tile is what the Map can stamp, and saving is where an editor-named tile asks before it takes a name it chose for you
do: Enter on site/floor, Escape, Enter on site/wall
press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if a prompt appears asking about the name, that is deliberate -- answer it and say whether the question made sense

steps.label: reopen it from the tiles
steps.goal: the tiles page lists what you have authored. Reopening lands you on the meshes page with the tile in hand, ready to edit
do: press left to come back to the tiles page if you are not already there
walk to the tile you just named
press Enter to reopen it
now press an arrow
steps.recovery: press left to come back out to the meshes page. If the arrow did nothing on the reopened tile, that is the report

steps.label: go to the Map and place a few pieces
steps.goal: the Map is the job -- the other tabs exist so this one can place things
do: press 1
arm a piece from the palette and click the ground a few times
steps.recovery: if nothing arms, the palette selection is empty -- walk it with the arrows first

steps.label: which way are you facing
steps.goal: the nav gizmo is new. It exists so that after orbiting the camera you can still answer 'which way is the wall facing' without guessing
do: orbit the camera around
look at the gizmo and say which way you think you are facing
then check it against a piece you know the orientation of
steps.recovery: if the gizmo is unreadable, or disagrees with the scene, say so -- and say where on the screen you expected it

steps.label: tip the brush over and fill a box with it
steps.goal: fixed this session and never walked by a person: a fill used to lay every row UPRIGHT however the brush was tipped, and stepped on the standing footprint so the rows overlapped. Both should now match what a single click of the same brush does
do: arm a wall
press Y a couple of times to tip it over (U tips the other axis)
click once on open ground to place one -- note how it lies
now drag a box out with the same brush and let go
steps.recovery: the two things to look at: are the filled pieces lying the same way as the one you clicked, and are the rows spaced so they do not intersect. Either being wrong is the report

steps.label: take some of it back
steps.goal: the removal box is locked to the same grid the fill lays on, so what the red box covers should be exactly what goes
do: press X to arm removal
drag a box over part of what you filled
let go
steps.recovery: if the box took more or less than it outlined, say which -- and roughly how much

steps.label: save the map
steps.goal: the end of the loop: what you built is on disk in a form the game reads
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to -- that message is the report
